title: NotificationRequestedV1
description:
Queue-only trigger contract (spec 10 §5) that crosses the broker from upstream producers (specs 06/09/11) to the notification consumer.

KEY DESIGN NOTES:
(a) notification_id is DERIVED by the consumer — not carried — as H(tenant, operation, event_type, recipient, template_version, material_revision). Redeliveries and republishes of the same logical event therefore always derive the same id and dedup (Inv-9).
(b) Implementation note: the concrete producers (spec 06/09) currently emit per-event message types — notification.booking_confirmed.v1, notification.booking_failed.v1, notification.still_confirming.v1, notification.user_action_required.v1, notification.alternatives_required.v1, notification.rejected.v1, notification.deposit_expired.v1, notification.waitlisted.v1 — which the ConsumerRegistry maps to this logical contract's event_type + priority.
(c) Carries no secrets, PAN, or CVV (Inv-12). recipient_ref is an opaque minimized handle; data_refs contains only safe reference tokens, never raw card data.

message_type.description: Explicit schema discriminator; always 'notification.requested.v1' for this contract.

tenant_id.description: Tenant scope. All consumer-side writes must be scoped to this tenant.

correlation_id.description: Correlation identifier propagated across all messages in an operation chain.

causation_id.description: message_id of the direct cause of this trigger (nullable — may be absent for synthetic or system-generated triggers).

operation_id.description: Stable operation identifier. Null only for non-operation messages (e.g. system-level administrative notifications). For all booking-lifecycle events this MUST be non-null as it is an identity input to notification_id derivation.

intent_revision.description: Material revision of the intent at the time the triggering state change committed. Forms part of the notification_id identity — a material intent change produces a new notification_id and a new logical notification (Inv-10).

event_type.description: Required-communication catalogue (spec 10 §18.4). Maps to NotificationEventType enum. Determines the message priority, template selection, and dedup identity.

recipient_ref.description: Opaque minimized recipient handle (e.g. recip_01...). NOT a raw phone number or email address in plaintext. The consumer dereferences this from the tenant-scoped recipient store to obtain the actual delivery destination. Carries no PAN/CVV (Inv-12).

template_hint.description: Advisory hint passed to the template resolver (e.g. 'booking_confirmed'). The resolver maps this to a concrete template_version that becomes part of the notification_id identity.

priority.description: Delivery priority aligning with MessagePriority enum. Governs the dispatch latency target (§8) and retry budget: critical ≤3 s p95, high ≤10 s p95, normal ≤30 s p95.

data_refs.description: Safe, non-secret reference data used by the template renderer. All fields are nullable. Never contains PAN, CVV, or raw payment credentials (Inv-12).

booking_id.description: Opaque booking identifier for template context (e.g. bk_01...). Present for booking-lifecycle events.

offer_expires_at.description: ISO-8601 with offset: deadline for a WaitlistOffer (§18.4). Null for all other event types. The Critical retry window for waitlist_offer must not exceed this value minus a safety margin (§8).

payment_link_token.description: Tokenized Stripe payment link reference for action_required (deposit, §09). Null for all other event types. This is a URL-safe token, never a PAN or CVV (Inv-12).
